pageCache.pageTitle: The Helix Education Centre - Promoting Fundamental British Values
pageCache.text:
Promoting Fundamental British Values
Promoting Fundamental British Values
In accordance with The Department for Education, The Helix Education Centre is committed to actively promote British values in schools to ensure young people leave school prepared for life in modern Britain. Pupils are encouraged to regard people of all faiths, races and cultures with respect and tolerance and understand that while different people may hold different views about what is ‘right’ and ‘wrong’, all people living in England are subject to its law.
The Key Values are:
We aim to support our children on their journey through life in developing and demonstrating skills and attitudes that will allow them to participate fully in and contribute positively to life in modern Britain.
The Helix Education Centre promotes British Values through the spiritual, moral, social and cultural education which permeates through the curriculum and supports the development of the ‘whole child’. We recognise that such development is most successful when those values and attitudes are promoted by all staff and provide a model of behaviour for our children.
Pupils are taught about democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty and mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs in the curriculum offered at The Helix, particularly PHSE/Citizenship and RE.
The Helix Education Centre values the importance of facilitating opportunities to be part of the community as the students, families and staff have much to offer in the development of community cohesion.

Help pupils to distinguish right from wrong

Welcome
WELCOME TO THE HELIX EDUCATION CENTRE
We are a service consisting of a Primary & Secondary Pupil Referral Unit, Hospital Education, Home Tuition, and an outreach Inclusion Support Team — providing education for pupils from 5–16 years, covering the four Key Stages. The Helix Education Centre supports pupils from all Harrow schools.
Our service provides transitional education and support for up to 160 learners per year when they are unable to attend mainstream school. Pupils enter the service when they have been permanently excluded, placed for respite, experiencing ill health (mental or physical), or occasionally due to other circumstances.
I do hope you find all the information you need from our website, or feel free to contact us for further details.

Welcome
ASPIRE - STUDY - PERSEVERE
Dear Parents and Carers,
I am writing to introduce myself as the new Interim Headteacher & Designated Safeguarding Lead at the Helix Education Centre.
It is both a privilege and a responsibility that I take very seriously, and I am excited to be working with you, your children, and our dedicated staff team.
The Helix Education Centre has a strong reputation for supporting young people to thrive in Harrow, often in the face of significant challenges. My priorities will be to ensure that every student feels safe, respected, and motivated to succeed. I believe that learning is most effective when schools and families work in partnership, and I am committed to building strong, open communication with you. Our School values of Aspire, Study and Persevere are integral to how we work at the Helix and I am sure we can help shape a positive journey for your child while they are with us.
Over the coming weeks, I look forward to getting to know our students, staff and families. I will be spending time in classrooms and around the centre to better understand the needs of our community. Please be assured that the wellbeing, progress, and future opportunities of your child will remain at the heart of every decision we make.
Your views are invaluable, and I welcome your support as we work together to provide the best possible education for our young people. My door is always open and if you have any questions then please feel free to contact me by phone, email or pop in for a coffee.
Thank you for your continued trust and partnership. I am confident that, together, we will continue to strengthen the positive and nurturing environment that makes the Helix Education Centre such a special place.
Andrew Burton Interim Headteacher The Helix Education Centre

pageCache.text:
Primary Curriculum
Key Stage 1 and 2 Curriculum
Primary pupils follow a broad and enriched curriculum following the National Curriculum 2014.
Our aim is to address pupils’ barriers to learning to enable them to make academic progress.
PRIMARY Subjects Taught
We focus on reading and writing with pupils learning through short texts. Early readers learn phonics and all pupils are heard read daily.
We focus on number and problem solving inclusive of place value, the four number operations and problem solving. Pupils are supported with equipment such as Base 10 Base 10 is the number system we use every day, where numbers are built using 10 digits (0–9) and each place value is 10 times bigger than the one before it. and practical activities including reading time.
Pupils also learn PSHE, Science, History or Geography, Computing, Art or DT, Food Technology and PE. Where possible, pupils learn through topics and links between subjects are made.
Other Information
Care is taken to maintain close links with parents/careers and associated educational providers.
If you require further information on our curriculum, please do not hesitate to speak to Helix staff.
Please look at this year’s curriculum plan so that you are able to see what your child will be learning by clicking the links below.

Pastoral Support
Education Support Workers (ESWs) Pastoral Support Offer
The ‘intent’ of our Pastoral Support is to enable our pupils to develop the required Behaviour for Learning for reintegration back to either mainstream school, Further Education or a Special provision.
Intent
The Education Support Workers’ (ESW) role in class is as Group Leaders and to support the teachers in providing differentiated teaching & learning or personalised learning for all pupils at the Helix. Additionally, the ESW’s role is to enable the pupils to access the breadth & depth of the curriculum appropriate to their abilities. And lastly, the ESWs are the first link between classroom and the pupils’ home.
Implementation
The initial keyworker session is used to re-affirm the Helix expectations (introduced at the pupil’s admission) and initial targets set.
Weekly keyworker sessions occur during which the Keyworker’s pro-forma is completed to address any key issues associated with:
We use SIMs to provide data for reports and progress data.
When a pupil is ready to be presented to Managed Move Committee (panel) the pupil’s Keyworker will work along the Transition Support Officer (TSO) to support the pupil to complete his or her personal statement and ensure all required documents are up to date.
Support the planning and delivery of lessons,
Attendance and Punctuality,
Personal – self management,
Social Interaction at the Helix,
